steps.action: MTA looks up MX records for example.com, opens a TCP:25 connection, runs STARTTLS, and walks the SMTP conversation. Blocking on network — this is the slow step.
steps.codeOrCommand:
mx = dns.query("example.com", "MX") # mx1.example.com pri=10
conn = smtp.connect("mx1.example.com", 25)
conn.starttls
conn.ehlo("mail-out.google.com")
conn.mail("<alice@gmail.com>")
conn.rcpt("<bob@example.com>")
conn.data( "Received: from... by mail-out.google.com...\r\n" + mime_bytes
)
→ 250 2.0.0 OK queued as 3F2504
steps.decision: remote accepted (250) — mark delivered. On 4xx → retry queue; on 5xx → bounce back to sender
steps.note: External SMTP is the slowest leg (50–500ms). We do NOT block the API response on it — MTA runs async after the 202.

steps.title: API returns 202 Accepted
steps.action: API replies immediately after the metadata+body writes succeed; MTA delivery runs asynchronously. Sent folder is already populated.
steps.codeOrCommand:
return Response(202, { "id": "01HZ8T7K4C-e4f2", "threadId": "t_447", "labelIds": ["SENT"]
})

steps.title: LB relays response
steps.action: Return path through the LB.

steps.title: UI moves draft to Sent
steps.action: Web app animates the message out of the compose window and appends it to the Sent folder view. Delivery-status pill remains 'sending' until a downstream MTA event confirms acceptance.

operations.title: Receive inbound email (MX → filters → inbox)
operations.name: Receive inbound email (MX → filters → inbox)
operations.description: Remote server delivers to our MX. Filter scores, metadata+body+attachments persist, recipient's inbox index updates, push notification fires.

steps.title: Remote MTA connects to our MX on port 25
steps.action: Sending server (mx.acme.co) opens SMTP, authenticates DKIM/SPF, and walks MAIL FROM / RCPT TO / DATA.
steps.codeOrCommand:
S: 220 gmail-smtp-in.l.google.com ESMTP
C: EHLO mx.acme.co
S: 250-STARTTLS...
C: STARTTLS
C: MAIL FROM:<charlie@acme.co>
C: RCPT TO:<bob@gmail.com>
C: DATA Received: from mx.acme.co by... DKIM-Signature: v=1; a=rsa-sha256; d=acme.co;... From: charlie@acme.co To: bob@gmail.com Subject: Contract v3... body + attachments....
S: 250 2.0.0 OK queued as m_aa71
steps.decision: SPF + DKIM pass — continue; on SPF hardfail we'd SMTP-reject with 550
steps.note: We buffer the DATA to disk before returning 250; this is the durability contract — once we ack we own it.

steps.title: Spam filter scores the inbound message
steps.action: Full inbound classification: sender reputation, Bayesian content, URL scan, attachment sandbox.
steps.codeOrCommand:
reputation = rep_lookup("acme.co", "198.51.100.9") # 0.87 (good)
content_score = nn_classifier.score(mime) # 0.12
urls_ok = safe_browsing.check(extract_urls(mime)) # attach_ok = sandbox.detonate(mime.attachments) # clean
score = combine(reputation, content_score, urls_ok, attach_ok)
if score > 0.9: return Disposition.SPAM # delivers to SPAM label, not INBOX
return Disposition.INBOX
steps.decision: score 0.08 < 0.9 — deliver to INBOX. Had it been > 0.9 we'd route to SPAM label; > 0.99 quarantines to an admin-only bucket

steps.title: Store attachment(s) content-addressed
steps.action: Hash each attachment; if hash already exists globally, just bump its refcount (dedupe). Otherwise PUT the bytes.
steps.codeOrCommand:
for part in mime.attachments: key = "sha256:" + sha256(part.bytes) if not blob.exists(key): blob.put(key, part.bytes, durability="3-way") blob.incref(key, owner="bob")
# For Contract.pdf:
# key = sha256:7c11...9bd
# already existed (charlie sent identical PDF last week) → no upload, just refcount++
steps.note: Content-addressing gives ~3x dedup savings across Gmail's corpus — big PDFs / viral CSVs are stored once.

steps.title: Store Bob's copy of the body
steps.action: Compressed body written under Bob's body key. Even though multiple recipients get the same RFC 822 bytes, we store one copy per recipient so per-user delete is trivial.
steps.codeOrCommand:
body_id = sha256("bob" || "m_aa71")
kv.put(body_id, zstd.compress(mime_body), durability="quorum")

steps.title: Insert into Bob's inbox shard
steps.action: Write the metadata row into Bob's partition, labels = INBOX.

steps.title: Indexer consumes CDC and updates Elasticsearch
steps.action: Change-data-capture stream pipes the metadata INSERT to an indexer worker which bulk-updates the user's shard in ES. Runs in parallel with the push notification.
steps.note: Index lag target < 5s p99 — during this window the message shows in inbox but is not yet findable via search.

steps.title: Push service notifies Bob's devices
steps.action: Spam filter emitted a `new_mail` event in parallel. Push service fans out to APNs / FCM / any live WebSocket for user=bob.
steps.codeOrCommand:
devices = device_registry.get("bob") # [apns:abc, fcm:xyz, ws:conn_413]
for d in devices: match d.kind: case "apns": apns.send(d.token, {"aps": {"alert": "Contract v3 — Charlie"}}) case "fcm": fcm.send(d.token,...) case "ws": ws.send(d.conn, {"event": "new_mail", "id": "m_aa71"})

operations.title: Search the inbox
operations.name: Search the inbox
operations.description: User types a query; API hits the search index filtered to their user id, hydrates hits with metadata, returns a ranked list.

steps.title: User types 'from:charlie invoice'
steps.action: Search bar issues a query after 300ms debounce.
steps.codeOrCommand:
GET /v1/messages:search?q=from%3Acharlie+invoice&maxResults=20 HTTP/1.1
Authorization: Bearer ya29.a0...

steps.title: LB forwards to API
steps.action: Round-robin pick — search is stateless.

steps.title: API translates to ES DSL
steps.action: API parses the Gmail-style query grammar and builds a bool query scoped to `user_id = bob`.
steps.codeOrCommand:
parsed = parse_gmail_query("from:charlie invoice")
# { must: [ {match: {from: "charlie"}},
# {match: {body: "invoice"}} ],
# filter: [ {term: {user_id: "bob"}} ] }
hits = search.query("mail-bob", parsed, size=20)

steps.title: Elasticsearch executes the query
steps.action: ES scatters the bool query across the user's shard replicas, ranks by BM25 + recency, returns the top 20 message_ids.

steps.title: API hydrates hits with metadata
steps.action: For the top 20 ids, API pulls full metadata rows (subject, snippet, labels, thread) from the user's partition.
steps.codeOrCommand:
SELECT message_id, thread_id, from_addr, subject, snippet, labels, received_at
FROM messages
WHERE user_id = 'bob' AND message_id IN ('m_aa71','m_8812',... )
USING CONSISTENCY LOCAL_ONE;

steps.title: API returns ranked result list
steps.action: API composes the final response: id, thread, snippet, and the matched-fields highlight returned by ES.
steps.codeOrCommand:
return Response(200, { "messages": [ {"id": "m_aa71", "threadId": "t_992", "snippet": "Bob — latest redlines attached...", "from": "charlie@acme.co", "subject": "Contract v3", "labelIds": ["INBOX","UNREAD"]},... ], "resultSizeEstimate": 14
})

steps.title: LB relays response
steps.action: Return path.

steps.title: Results render in the search dropdown
steps.action: Typical end-to-end latency 40–100ms — fast enough for live type-ahead.

tradeoffs.decision: Synchronous spam rejection at SMTP vs post-accept filtering
tradeoffs.chosen: Accept-and-tag with a spam score, move to SPAM label if over threshold
tradeoffs.rationale: Rejecting at SMTP time sends a permanent failure that senders see as a bounce. False positives are catastrophic for legitimate mail; accepting and hiding is reversible and gives users a Spam folder to audit.

tradeoffs.decision: Metadata and body in the same row vs split storage
tradeoffs.chosen: Split: metadata in SQL, body in content-addressed KV, attachments in blob store
tradeoffs.rationale: Users scroll metadata ~100x more than they open bodies. A 50 KB body in the metadata row would multiply read bandwidth by 100. Splitting keeps inbox-list p95 at ~50 ms and lets attachments dedupe across recipients.

tradeoffs.chosen: Async CDC pipeline with ~5 s target staleness
tradeoffs.rationale: A strongly consistent inline index would couple write latency to the slowest index shard and is not worth it for a feature where 5 s staleness is imperceptible. CDC also lets us rebuild the index from the source of truth on schema changes.

tradeoffs.chosen: Shard by user_id (hash) with per-user locality
tradeoffs.rationale: All inbox operations are per-user, so a hash on user_id gives local reads and writes, no cross-shard queries on the hot path, and even distribution. Hot celebrity users can be isolated onto dedicated shards.

tradeoffs.decision: Push delivery: persistent WebSocket vs mobile push gateway
tradeoffs.chosen: WebSocket for web, APNs/FCM for mobile
tradeoffs.rationale: Mobile OSes kill background sockets within seconds; a native push gateway is the only reliable way to reach a backgrounded app. Web apps stay with WebSockets because they are foregrounded when it matters.
